name: Paid election worker (municipal, provincial or federal elections)
summary: Short-term paid jobs staffing voting places for municipal, provincial or federal elections; hiring happens in the weeks or months before each vote.
whatYouDo: After a short paid training session, you work at a voting location on advance-poll days or election day, greeting voters, checking registration, issuing ballots or supervising. Days often run 12-14 hours, and the election office decides your assignment.
appeal: Paid training (Elections Canada pays about 3 hours)
No experience needed for entry roles
Elections Canada accepts online applications at any time; age 16+ for federal elections
Ontario municipal examples: $225-$300/day plus $50-$60 for training in Windsor-Essex (news); Toronto lists about $280 for one role
watchOuts: Very long days (12-14 hours) on site
Work exists only around elections, so it is sporadic
Toronto's hiring for the October 26, 2026 municipal election is closed (positions filled); other cities' training ran late September-early October, so this cycle is likely too late
Must stay non-partisan; candidates, their families and campaign workers are excluded
Eligibility differs: federal requires Canadian citizenship and age 16+; Toronto requires 18+ and legal right to work
Federal pay rates differ between Elections Canada pages and years; check the current rate

training.notes: Mandatory training; Elections Canada pays about 3 hours; Toronto training about 2.5 hours; Windsor-Essex pays $50-$60.

compensation.notes: Varies by election and role. Elections Canada pages: roughly $20-$27/hr (one page), $27.76 for central poll supervisor (another); 2025 news: $17.40-$33.08/hr. Ontario municipal 2026 examples: $225-$300/day (Windsor-Essex news), about $280 (Toronto).

reliability.notes: Only during election periods; next federal/provincial dates depend on when elections are called.

applicationSteps: Federal: apply online at elections.ca/jobs (accepted any time); you are contacted when an election is called
Municipal or provincial: watch your city clerk's or Elections Ontario's site in the months before a vote
Work your assigned advance-poll or election-day shift
fitsIf: You want occasional, short, in-person paid work, can handle long days and can stay politically neutral.
notFitIf: You need regular income or remote work, or cannot manage a 13-14 hour day on site.
